page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.3xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at 2.5 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage or dedicated GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance divergence between single-threaded and multi-threaded workloads. Single-core CPU performance is weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% tiers. Single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also register poor performance. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by middle-tier scores in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth remains average, though the overall PassMark memory score is weak.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-core performance, this instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads that do not require high single-core throughput or massive memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, and moderate database operations. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications or single-threaded processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable multi-threaded compute resources, though the lack of local storage and lower single-core performance are notable tradeoffs.
